review_note: Preserve association language and institutional criticism; cut self-praise and an unnecessary retrospective justification.

edits.before: Self-advocacy is associated with better educational and employment outcomes --- which is why week 8 teaches it, and why week 8 refuses to stop there.
edits.after: A mini-review of associations between self-advocacy, self-determination and outcomes for autistic adolescents and young adults.
edits.reason: Let the description identify the reading rather than advertise the course's principled response.

edits.before: The hedge in that phrasing is the authors' own and the week keeps it: these are associations reported in a short review, not a demonstrated effect of teaching anybody to write an email.
edits.after: These are associations reported in a short review, not a demonstrated effect of teaching somebody to write an email.
edits.reason: Preserve the limit without praising the course for reproducing it.

edits.before: Week 8 uses this to justify spending an hour on institutional scripts at all. Asking well is associated with outcomes that matter, so the skill is worth having. Read beside Davies & Bagnall, though, it sets up the week's real position: self-advocacy helps the person doing it, *and* a system that works only for students who can do it has pushed its own cost onto them.
edits.after: Read beside Davies & Bagnall in week 8: teach the script, and ask why access to support depends on the student knowing how to ask.
edits.reason: Keep the institutional criticism and practical implication in one sentence.
